newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pepkor sells Walhold, Waltons stakes.
newsitem.headline: Pepkor sells Walhold, Waltons stakes.

text.p: South African retailing group Pepkor said on Tuesday it had sold its holdings in office supplies group Walhold and its subsidiary Waltons Stationery Co for 408 million rand to Investec and an institutional investor

Investec paid 9.68 rand per share for the 15 percent Pepkor held directly in Waltons and 9.35 rand per share for the 34.9 percent held in Walhold (Waltons Consolidated Investment Holdings Ltd), Pepkor said in a statement
Pepkor's remaining 18.2 percent interest in Walhold was taken up by an unnamed institutional investor.

The Bidvest Group Ltd, who had offered to buy Walton's business, paid Pepkor 39 million rand cash in terms of a restraint of trade agreement prohibiting Pepkor from entering into competition with business currently undertaken by Waltons for two years.
"Pepkor's total income from the transaction consequently amounted to 447.1 million rand, which represents a significant profit on its original investment," it said
Pepkor chairman Christo Wiese said his group had decided to sell its interest in Walhold and Waltons to focus on other expansion opportunities opening up for the group in Africa and abroad.
